evidence_excerpts: Representative pictures from fMRI and other neuroimaging methods do not clearly convey the complex chain of biological and computational steps that lead to inferences about brain structure and function.
Many neuroimaging studies have used cross-sectional designs, precluding possible inferences about underlying cause-and-effect relationships.
text: Neuroimaging evidence on meditation can suggest modest brain differences, but group averages, cross-sectional designs, cardiorespiratory artifacts, head motion, and interpretive oversimplification limit causal and practical conclusions.
